transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that I just can't seem to turn off the worrying once it starts. 

I mean, I'll tell myself I’ve made the list, checked the dates, and done absolutely everything I reasonably can... but my mind just keeps going anyway. It's just getting a bit tiring.

When you find yourself worrying, is it usually focused on a specific fear, such as being judged by others or a need to perform certain rituals, or is it more of a general, constant concern about many different aspects of your daily life?

It's definitely more of a general concern. I don't really worry about being judged by people, and I don't have any rituals I need to do. 

My mind just keeps roaming from one thing to the next. Like, I'll be thinking about an upcoming exhibition schedule, and then that turns into worrying about my daughter's travel plans, or... or whether the house gutters need fixing. It's just everyday stuff, really. But these small things start to feel as if they could unravel into something much bigger, even when I know they probably won't.
Over what period of time have you been experiencing these persistent worries on more days than not?

Well, I'd say it's been going on for about seven months now. It started... shortly after a friend of mine passed away. I was trying to step in and keep the projects we had been working on moving forward, and I suppose the worrying just picked up around then and hasn't really stopped since.
Beyond the constant worrying, have you been experiencing any physical symptoms, such as muscle tension, feeling restless, or difficulty getting a good night's sleep?

Well, yes, actually. I definitely notice the muscle tension. By the time evening rolls around, my shoulders and my neck are just so tight. It's like I've been walking around bracing myself all day long. I even catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes when I'm just sitting down trying to read, or... or when I'm planning out the activities for the garden center. It's just this constant tightness.
Do you find that you feel easily fatigued or have trouble focusing on your tasks because your mind goes blank or drifts off?

Yes, I definitely feel fatigued. Even when I manage to sleep through the whole night, I wake up feeling as if I have already put in half a day. It's quite draining. 

Just doing normal things takes it out of me... like, by the time I water the garden beds or sort out the papers for my book club, I really need to sit down and just gather myself. I haven't really noticed my mind going blank or having trouble focusing, though. It's mostly just feeling so tired all the time.
Do you find yourself becoming irritable more easily than you used to?

No, I wouldn't say so. I haven't really noticed feeling irritable or short-tempered. Even with being so tired lately, I don't think I'm snapping at anyone or getting frustrated more easily than usual. It's really just the worrying and the exhaustion.
When you are in bed at night, do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

No, I don't really have trouble with that. I usually fall asleep just fine, and I tend to stay asleep through the night. It's just that when I wake up, I don't feel rested at all. But the actual sleeping part doesn't seem to be an issue.
